properties.comments: The site is an the end of a valley, which means there is air coming right in front of you as soon as breeze is starting to blow : you can fly here during hours in the valley breeze. It's a very good site to learn soaring. It's very easy to go up, it's usually frequented by acro pilots for this reason.
properties.weather:
Worlwide known acro site. Is a place where thermals can be real strong on hot days, so be careful in the hot hours of the afternoon.  Also when the conditions are strong, care must be taken not to fall off to the back of the mountain since there's venturi effect there which accelerates the wind and also in the ridges to the east. A good rule of thumb will be not go northern past the antennas on the top unless you have quite a lot of altitude above them. So if the conditions are strong the best is to stay well on the face of the mountain. Landing options are not appealing in case one can't return to the valley and land north. Going down is easy, just fly south above the village and soon you'll get into the descendence. It's called the 'magic mountain' for a reason ;)
Also keep an eye for too much cloud development. The weather can change rather quickly. The pre-storm gusts can be dangerous.

landing.landing_description: Can be turbulent, specially in the southern part near the trees and the river, so it's better to land closer to the mountain and piloting actively to counter any collapses at low altitude.

properties.comments: This is the main launch site that is usable on 90 percent of good flyable days. There is a car park, a bar (not is use, and vandalised since 2001) and the take off area is divided into two sections: above and below the road. With nil wind it is generally better to take off below the road as it is steeper and if there is any danger of catabatic wind it affect the upper take off first. With a few km/hr of wind, the top take of is used. There is a fence to the rear, so if there is any chance of you being dragged back on a failed take off, it is best to prepare a little down slope. If you top land, the best area is the flatter area near the windsock on the west side of the upper launch. The whole area is a little rocky, and also there are a number of gorse bushes. We have been clearing the site by hand, improving it as best we can. For 2009 a significant improvement is anticipated with help of the local government and town hall with a budget of 31.000 euros.

East to West you can easily break the 100km mark, some local pilots are close to breaking the 200km barrier. Plus the weather can be counted on to be excellent in Spring Summer and even Autumn.

properties.name: Ager
properties.takeoff_description:
There are 4 takeoffs:

lowest take off is RAUDORAL.
Recently created, it allows take off without going all the way up to the top of the Montsec.Its a clean fairly steep takeoff that take a single paralider (while another prepares). It is faced South and is the first take off that comes the breeze while the slope is heated. BEWARE OF EAST WIND when we do not recommend use. Height to the Camping landing field: 500 m.
GPS: 31T 312693, 4656422

- GABRIELO.
It is a take off with a spacious zone to put the hang gliders and paragliders. We take off only for one point, and we should look all the streamers, because it is a technical take off. It is South faced, and not suitable with West winds. It is a good take off when the North wind on the top of Montsec. Height to Ager: 550m.
GPS: 31T 315102, 4655761

MAIN TOP TAKE OFF COLL D'ARES.
It is very big and clear take off. It has a few streamers to show the wind. It is South faced, but it allows to take off with West winds. If there is East wind, it is slightly in rotor. In an east it's better to continue to the Sant Alis take off. The height to Ager is 960 m. 
GPS: 31T 313555 , 4657599

- SANT ALIS.
It is geodesic vertex. It offers an incredible view: The Montseny, Moncayo, Guara mountain range, Pyrenees from Navarra to Girona, Montserrat, Monte Caro, Prades and Montsant mountain range. The take off is just on the left and in front of the firewatch cabin. It is South-East faced. Don't use with West winds. The height to Ager is 1050 m.
GPS: 31T 315237, 4656809
properties.going_there:
From Barcelona (2h far & 180Km):
A2 Lleida direction - Martorell - Igualada - Tarrega - Balaguer - cross river Balaguer sharp right - take C-12 - Les Avellanes - Font de pou - Ager.
properties.comments:
Perfect area for beginners pilots to XC pilots.
Massive take off and landings!
Holding a PWC competition in 2007 and many competitions in the past (Hang gliding world championship, Paragliding British Open 2006, National championships, etc...)

We have a great road to take off. We have an emergency helicopter 5 minutes away in Tremp.

Lovely small town feel. Great for a Spanish Holiday with tapas, sun and swimming.

We have loads of other out door activities like Kyaks,rock climbing, walking, mountain biking (7 euros half a day hire), Quad bikes, Tandem flights, light aircraft flight. We have a great new observatory which is open to the public on week ends http://www.parcastronomic.cat/

landing.landing_description:
- Vertet Landing Field.
It is near the Camping Vall d'Ager. There is a sign befor the oange fuel station opposite the 'Bar Torres'. It is a rectangular field of 200 x 50 m., West - East oriented. It now has wood beams in the parking lot. Carefull with the turbulence of the trees with North wind and if in trouble use any of the other massive landing options nearby. Wind sock on top id the campsite that also has flags.
GPS: 31T 315079 , 4652814

- Cal Maciarol Landing Field.
One of the biggest of the valley. It's near the road to the take off. Good for all wind directions. It has all the services: Bar, accomodation, paragliding school and shop...take care with power line on Main road Its a really good option with a pig farm. It has an small aeroplane that also uses the landing and lands towards the hill in a North direction. Nice big wind sock and streamer.

- ALTERNATIVE LANDING FIELD. (known by 300's field)
Is a landing field situated in front of the take off 'Coll d'Ares'. They are one height more or less than 300 m. from the take off . It is used when not enough height to get to the valley.

Ager valley has many great landing fields. Please respect crops in the field and no smoking in the fields in Summer as its Fire risk.

properties.name: Chia
properties.takeoff_description:
Statistics

    * Altitude 1800 metres (5850 feet) ASL
    * Top to bottom height: 400 metres (1300 feet)
    * Orientations S and SE

Access

From the south side of the Chia pass there is a dirt track which leads to both launches.

South East launch: This is in the bowl facing ESE. Parking near the water container, you walk 80 m up the hill were there is a large grassy launch, suitable for easy top landings.

Southerly launch: follow the track out of the bowl to the main southerly face. Take off is a very shallow grassy area which is safe and easy for top landing.
properties.flight_rules: Little used site, but essential on stronger SE days when the wind fails to come in at PN. On these days give good evening flying.  Beware flying here on strong wind strong thermal days mid afternoon.
properties.going_there: You drive up the Chia pass from the Piedrahita (Corneja) valley.  You will go through Villafranca and Navacepedilla de Corneja.  about 50m after going over the pass there is a forest road on the right.
properties.comments: This is an excellent easy site, which offers good ridge soaring in the evening when restitution often sets up. We often go to this site when the wind is over the back at early in the day at PeÃ±a Negra. If pilots have not climbed out by around 2pm, we will often return PeÃ±a Negra. It is common to go over the back at Chia and find convergence with the anabatic wind up the face of the Piedrahita range. We have had some excellent XC flights from here to Salamanca and Cuidad Rodrigo.
properties.weather:
This site can take a lot of southerly wind witha degree of safety (slightly rising grazing land behind reduce rotor effects.
Often the base can be low and raining in the Piedrahita valley, and flyable in Chia.  It is a place you can often fly when on a day which starts to overdevelop, since Cbs generally form at other points around it.  However, you still need to go and land when they get big as they can break into the Chia valley

landing.landing_description: Out front of the S launch is very flat, with many unfenced large fields. We normally land in the large field with the goalposts. From the SE take off you sometimes do not reach the football field. There is a suitable landing field next to the road going down.

properties.name: La Lastra del Cano
properties.takeoff_description:
Statistics

    * Altitude: 1.625 metres (5281 feet) ASL
    * Top to Bottom height: 500 metres (1625 feet)
    * Orientation : S and W
properties.flight_rules: Restricted flying untill August due to nesting black vultures.
properties.going_there: From in front of the bar of the village of Lastra del Cano there is a forestry track. After 400m there is a gate, which maybe closed by the people in the fire watchtower. The principal (S) take off is about 4km along the track. There is also a good west face below the Watchtower(W), the but presence of Black Vultures prevents its use during much of the season.
properties.comments:
This is an epic site. For a time in the 1995 it held a huge number of national distance to goal flights (after a goal of 170km to Arcones in the PWC). The European record has been achieved at this site on 3 occasions.

The take off is a grassy slope, in a large clearing in the pine forest which covers most off the hill. There is always a smell of wild Lavender and thyme, and the view out front toward the Gredos mountains and the river Tormes below are fantastic. On a day when we fly here it means that the wind is too strong from the south for the anabatic wind to come up the PeÃ±a Negra launch (on unstable days, southerly winds of more than 20km/hr can be stopped by the valley breeze at PeÃ±a Negra). Unless you get away early, the conditions can become too strong to take off. During the evening conditions usually lighten and provide excellent smooth ridge lift, occasionally with usable wave from the Gredos in front.

The face of the hill is steep, and has many granite fingers and ledges where the Griffon Vultures nest. When we fly here there are always vultures to accompany us.
properties.weather: On any good day with light winds the wind will also come on at PeÃ±a Negra (Piedrahita),  If it is a south windday the anabatic wind can get very strong early on.

landing.landing_description: Lastra is a spine backed ridge, so it is easy to go over the back and land on the main N-110 highway where there are plenty of large easy fields. Normally on an evening flight we will all Â¨go over the backÂ¨ and try to get to as close to Piedrahita as possible along the main road. In front of the hill the fields are generally smaller fields and though they are generally easy for a paragliders, they can cause some stress for hang glider pilots.

properties.name: Jabalcon (Zujar)
properties.takeoff_description:
The NW takeoff is very large and located at the very top of the hill.  No serious hazards apart from the masts behind.  Ridge to the right of takeoff is apparently a good thermal trigger.

The Southerly takeoff is has been manicured for paragliding but does require very committed launch.  People tended to head straight to the huge rock face to the right of takeoff.  

Never flown easterly, very intimidating launch.  Only enough room for one glider and maybe four or five steps.
properties.going_there: Head to the small town of Zujar, near to Baza.  Go down the main street.  Take a right hand turn that leads straight up to the hill.  When on the track up the hill.  The NW and S takeoffs are on a sharp left hand bend that then winds past both.  I think the E takeoff you just carry on straight up the original track.

properties.weather: Sometimes rough convergences can develop later in the day.

properties.going_there:

After Igualada, take exit 545 to Calaf, and follow that direction (turn left just after the exit).
After a while, you'll be climbing the hill with all the windmills. At the top, on your right, there's a dirtroad. Follow it untill you see a small cross in stone on the edge of the hill, the take off is there, park near the windmill.
properties.comments:
Site used mostly from May to October, when the marine breeze enters at the end of the day.
However, with meteo wind from the south, it may work other periods of the year, but chances are smaller.
Easy to see with all the windmills.
properties.weather: You have to fly with wind from S or SW. Wind can be too strong to fly.

landing.landing_description:
Top landing possible and recommended, but following this approach : you have to come from the west, i.e. have the windmills on your left, fly over the takeoff which should be then on your right, make a U turn and then land. 
Despite what you may think, there are no turbulences at all, and toplanding is usually nice and easy.

If top landing is not possible (not enough wind), it is possible to land on the dirtroad 200m below, that you can see if you look from the cross.

properties.flight_rules: ...Las habituales. No dejar vehículos obstaculizando maniobras y/o accesos a caminos secundarios ni despoerdigados por el monte. Mejor dejarlos aparcados a la orilla en el camino y subir los últimos 50m a pie.

A un par de kilómetros a la derecha se encuentra una campa donde solemos dejar coches y usamos como aterrizaje oficial. Es fácil distinguirla aun cuando no haya mangas. El camino sigue asfaltado hasta una curva pronunciada a derecha, en el punto donde se pasa a la otra cara de la ladera. Nosotros tomamos curva a derecha para no cambiarnos de cara y seguimos por camino de tierra de estado irregular. Se puede subir turismos pero con muidado en los bajos y sin prisa ni mucho peos. Mejor furgos y TT. Otra opción es seguir por asfalto hasta el pueblo Zenzano (tras el despegue) y subir a pata unos 20 minutos.
properties.comments:
Zona de vuelo LER99 afectada por restricciones del aeropuerto civil y del militar, ambos en Agoncillo. Restricciones habituales : No volar entre semana antes de las 15:00 (posibles maniobras de helicópteros militares en la zona) Restricciones adicionales: Consultar NOTAM.
Adicionalmente y en caso de no haber restricciones, llamar a torre civil aeropuerto para dejar constancia de nuestra presencia indicando número de pilotos, zona de vuelo y horarios.
properties.weather: Se vuela con vientos de componente Norte y Oeste. Termoladera que funicona mejor a partir de las 15:00. Techos no muy altos, 2.200m de media. El mejor vuelo de distancia, ganando el llano por encima del aterrizaje oficial para poder luego aprovechar deriva siun que ésta nos meta en las sierras cercanas. Puede entrar el Norte fuerte a última hora en el despegue y casi seguro que se disparen Nortes o Noresetes en la duiirección antural del cross, conviente estar atento.

properties.takeoff_description: Poniente Take-off = 36.8952, -5.4157 – 900m
properties.going_there:
A-384 out of Algodonales direction West: turn right, soon after the Cespa garage, then right towards La Muela after a few kilometres there is a right hand turning, keep heading for after La Muela. After a few hundred metres you pass the LZ for 'Poniente'… check the windsock and look around; it is not the most pleasant place to land due to the trees, valley and power lines. After La Muela, there is a gateway on the right to the picnic area and there is a sign: to the Launch Sites (from here on road is unpaved, rough, winding and often narrow, but no problem for 2WD, but watch out for returning vans!). 
If coming from 'Olvera' you can drive more directly to launch by taking the right turn towards 'la Muela' (CA-9101): turn-off after Olvera, at 36.9436033,-5.3086977, then as. 
Hiking to launch(es) is also possible and often done from the Poiniente Landing site,  la Muela and Algodonales.
properties.comments:
Excellent site for all kinds of pilots; summer months thermal activity is heavy, but evening flights are good. But then few are here anyway, as it's too hot with temperatures sometimes above 45°C between late June to early September. 

Poniente works well in the afternoon and evenings when Lavante stops.

There are several companies offering instruction and guiding in the town… it is a lively and fun place in season (spring and autumn).
